evidence.note: New HTTP/mock judge reviewed in full against the task-done rubric: no eval, no TODO/FIXME, no truncated context, no duplicated inventoried path.
Var substitution, command pinning and consent digest reviewed; verified against internal/fsm/workflow/workflow.go and internal/fsm/machine/machine.go rather than from the diff alone.
Typed FoldError/StoreError codes and CodeFor mapping; Unwrap exposes the cause for ERR_APPEND_REJECTED.
Version 0.8.2 to 0.9.0; cross-checked package.json, .claude-plugin/plugin.json, .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, .codex-plugin/plugin.json and CHANGELOG.md - all read 0.9.0, consistent.

Golden proves the nonce fence is sound: FenceBlock JSON-marshals the payload, so untrusted text carrying <<<END-<nonce> stays inside one quoted line and cannot close the fence, and {{1}}/{diff} in the value are not rescanned by format().

Validation evidence: go vet ./internal/fsm/... ./internal/version/ is clean, and go test -cover reports 100.0% of statements for internal/fsm/judge, internal/fsm/workflow and internal/fsm/run, so every source file in this shard has relevant tests.

Checked the caller-var-into-argv risk from Resolve/ResolveCmds: init refuses unless AllowCustomCmds equals the resolved cmds_sha256, and fork.go:192 repeats the check, so a var that rewrites argv[0] still needs fresh human consent. Not a finding.

Checked the empty-argv panic suspicion at resolve.go argv[0]: parse rejects argv outside 1..MaxArgv, and collectRefs (workflow.go:603) rejects any undeclared $VAR in model/effort/params/argv, so Resolve cannot silently substitute an unknown var. Not a finding.

findings.note: checkURL never rejects a hostless base URL: url.Parse("https://") yields scheme https with an empty Host and passes every guard, so a typo in ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL/OPENAI_BASE_URL produces "https:///v1/messages", which Do rejects as a transport error and the ladder retries all 5 attempts (1+2+4+8s of sleep) before surfacing what is really a fatal configuration error. A u.Host == "" check beside the userinfo check would fail it fast at New/Preflight time.

evidence.note: checkURL validates userinfo, path, query, fragment and scheme, but not that a host is present.

findings.note: attempt() discards the http.NewRequestWithContext error (hreq, _ := ...) and immediately dereferences hreq for Header.Set, so any request-construction failure is a nil-pointer panic rather than a typed ERR_JUDGE_* error. Currently unreachable because checkURL already url.Parse-es the base and the method is a constant, which is presumably why the branch is elided to keep 100% statement coverage - but the failure mode is a panic, not an error, if that ever stops holding.

evidence.note: hreq, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(...) followed by hreq.Header.Set on the next line.

findings.note: Verdict.Attempts is incremented at the top of the loop, before the backoff wait, so a context cancellation during the sleep returns a Verdict claiming one more attempt than was actually sent. The count is audited (LLMCallData is built from the Verdict in internal/fsm/cli/run.go), so the audit trail overstates attempts by one on every cancelled call. Setting v.Attempts after the backoff select would fix it.

evidence.note: v.Attempts = attempt + 1 precedes the select on ctx.Done()/clock.After at lines 499-503.

findings.note: Resolve substitutes $VAR only in string and []any params; a nested map[string]any param falls into the default branch and is copied verbatim, and paramRefs (workflow.go:638) has the same blind spot, so such a $VAR is neither validated as declared nor substituted and would reach the kind as the literal text "$JUDGE". Latent only: every kind registered today allows either no params or the single int param "lenses" (kind.go:260 validateLenses, kind.go:325 noParams), so no current workflow can hit it. Worth either recursing into maps or rejecting non-scalar params at parse time before a future kind accepts one.

evidence.note: default branch assigns nn.Params[k] = v without substitution.
node.Params[k] = v accepts any YAML value, including a nested mapping.

findings.note: The calibration pin is only as strong as the workflow's use of $JUDGE: Resolve pins JUDGE/JUDGE_EFFORT among declared vars, and judge.validate independently enforces effort == medium under calibration, but nothing pins the model, so a node with a hardcoded model (say model: claude-opus-5) runs a calibration run against a non-reference judge while still being stamped Calibration in the audit. Note that validate also skips the Anthropic unknown-family check when calibration is set, so the hardcoded path is not even family-checked. Either refuse a calibration init whose resolved node models differ from CalibrationJudge, or state in the doc comment that hardcoded models are out of the pin's scope.

evidence.note: pins map applies only to declared vars named JUDGE/JUDGE_EFFORT.
validate enforces the calibration effort pin and skips the family check under calibration, but never checks the model against the reference judge.

findings.note: Dead statement in the Anthropic legacy thinking branch: delete(body, "temperature") is immediately followed by body["temperature"] = 1, so the delete has no observable effect on the marshalled body. Harmless, but it reads as if the intent was to drop temperature entirely and the following line contradicts it.

evidence.note: delete(body, "temperature") then body["temperature"] = 1 on the next line.
